_note: The answers on the site on 15 November 2026, for the near-miss writers: id, pages, questions as worded on the site, short answer, its main catch. `part`: 707 writes part 1, 708 writes part 2. `skip`: answers about routes, onset or amounts that get no wordings.

questions: Can drinking lots of water on MDMA lead to low blood salt?
answers.short: Possibly. Low blood salt (sodium) after MDMA has been reported, mostly in young people; of 17 UK cases, at least 10 had drunk a lot of liquid.
answers.but: These only count people who got ill. So they can't show how often it happens, or whether drinking more changes the risk.

questions: Is ecstasy really MDMA, and how strong are the pills?
answers.short: Often, but not always. In European pill tests in 2009, 19 to 64 in 100 pills held MDMA, depending on the country. By 2013 most did, and held more of it.
answers.but: These were pills people chose to bring in, and the newest tests are from 2013. Pills today may be different.

questions: What happens when cocaine and alcohol are used together?
Cocaine with alcohol: what happens to the heart?
answers.short: Together they make a new substance, cocaethylene, and hearts beat faster than with cocaine alone.
answers.but: Small hospital studies of 8 and 6 people. None measured heart attacks or rhythm problems.

questions: Can cocaine make someone feel less drunk?
Does cocaine hide how drunk someone is?
answers.short: People given cocaine with alcohol did not feel more drunk, and sometimes slightly less.
answers.but: This is second-hand from one review of small studies, and no one tested driving.

questions: Why can the usual amount be dangerous after a break?
answers.short: Because tolerance may drop during a break, reviews say. In one study, 3 people died of an overdose after a hospital detox. All 3 had stayed for the whole programme.
answers.but: Nobody measured anyone's tolerance. And it's 3 deaths in one small study.

questions: What do people do when a strip shows fentanyl?
answers.short: Some say they use less or go slower; many keep the same amount.
answers.but: This is what people said or planned. Nobody watched what they actually did.

questions: Do people who use test strips have fewer overdoses?
answers.short: No one knows yet. One study found no clear difference over four weeks.
answers.but: The result was too uncertain to rule out fewer or more overdoses.

questions: What does ketamine do to perception, thinking and the sense of self while it is working?
What does ketamine do to perception, thinking and sense of self?
answers.short: Compared with a salt-water day, people felt cut off from themselves and their thinking got muddled.
answers.but: Raters could probably tell who had ketamine, and the studies disagree a lot about how big the effects are.

questions: How does ketamine work in the brain?
answers.short: It blocks a docking point for the brain's main go-signal, called the NMDA receptor.
answers.but: Nearly all these numbers come from animals and from cells in dishes, and reach us through reviews.

questions: Do people who use cannabis often do worse on memory and thinking tests?
answers.short: On average they score a little lower than people who use little or none.
answers.but: People were tested only after they had started, so the studies can't show that cannabis caused it.

questions: Do memory and thinking differences last after people stop using cannabis?
answers.short: Not clear. Where studies asked people to stop for over 3 days, the gap was small.
answers.but: This compared different studies, not the same people before and after they stopped.

questions: Does using cannabis as a teenager lower IQ later in life?
answers.short: Not shown either way. In one study, people dependent for years lost about 6 IQ points.
answers.but: Other differences between people could explain it. Twin studies of lighter use found no clear extra loss.

questions: Is teenage cannabis use linked to depression or anxiety later?
answers.short: Teens who used cannabis the most were a bit more often depressed later than teens who didn't.
answers.but: These studies can't show that cannabis caused it; other differences between the teens may explain it.

questions: Is teenage cannabis use linked to suicidal thoughts or attempts?
answers.short: Teens who used cannabis the most reported suicidal thoughts or attempts more often than teens who didn't.
answers.but: Only three studies each, mostly measured in the teen years; they cannot show cause.

questions: Is using cannabis in pregnancy linked to a smaller baby, early birth or intensive care?
Is cannabis in pregnancy linked to smaller babies or intensive care?
answers.short: Babies were a bit lighter, and more of them went to intensive care after birth.
answers.but: Many mothers also smoked or drank. Most studies could not tell this apart from cannabis.

questions: Is cannabis linked to heart attacks and strokes?
answers.short: Some studies link it to heart attacks and strokes; a 25-year study found no link.
answers.but: These figures come from reviews. The studies could not fully tell cannabis and tobacco apart.

questions: Do cannabis medicines help long-lasting pain?
answers.short: Slightly: about half a point less pain out of 10 than with a dummy medicine.
answers.but: The trials were short, mostly tested one mouth spray, and many had weaknesses.

questions: Do cannabis medicines ease muscle stiffness in multiple sclerosis (MS)?
answers.short: People felt a little less stiff than with a dummy, but doctors' tests showed no clear change.
answers.but: The trials were short, most often tested one mouth spray, and many had weaknesses.

questions: Do cannabis medicines help with sickness from chemotherapy?
answers.short: In three small trials, more people had their sickness fully controlled than with a dummy.
answers.but: Only 102 people were in these three trials, and most trials had weaknesses.

questions: Do cannabis medicines help sleep, anxiety, appetite or other conditions?
answers.short: Too few small trials to tell; sleep scores were slightly better than with a dummy.
answers.but: Each condition had only a few small trials. Many had serious weaknesses.

questions: What side effects do cannabis medicines cause?
answers.short: More side effects than with a dummy, such as dizziness, feeling high, confusion and dry mouth.
answers.but: Short trials at the highest dose tested; long-term harms were not studied.

questions: How many people who use cannabis become dependent on it?
answers.short: About 9 in 100 people who ever tried it, in two older US surveys.
answers.but: The surveys are from 1990 to 2005 and used a narrower definition than today's.

questions: Are frequent use and starting young linked to cannabis dependence?
answers.short: People who use more often are more often dependent; for starting young, studies disagree.
answers.but: Most numbers come second-hand from reviews, and none can show what causes what.

questions: How common is withdrawal when people who use cannabis regularly stop, and what is it like?
How common is cannabis withdrawal, and what is it like?
answers.short: About 17 in 100 in general surveys; more than half in clinic and hospital groups.
answers.but: Studies counted it in different ways, and none checked how often people get these feelings anyway.

questions: What is cannabis hyperemesis syndrome (repeated severe vomiting), and does stopping end it?
answers.short: Bouts of severe vomiting with regular cannabis use; in reported cases, stopping ended them.
answers.but: Published cases only: nobody knows how common it is, and fewer than half were followed up.

questions: How does THC move through the body after smoking and after eating, and how long does it stay in blood and urine?
How fast does THC rise and fall in the blood, smoked or eaten?
answers.short: Smoked, THC peaks in the blood within minutes; eaten, it rises slowly over hours.
answers.but: Old, small lab studies of weak cannabis, described in one review.

questions: Can cannabis cause psychosis, and does using it daily matter?
answers.short: People who use cannabis, most of all daily, get psychosis more often than people who don't.
answers.but: This is a link: these studies cannot show that cannabis was the cause.

questions: Is strong cannabis more closely linked to psychosis than weaker cannabis?
answers.short: Daily use of strong types had the strongest link with psychosis, but the gap from weaker types could be chance.
answers.but: Strength was guessed from the type people named, and both studies come from one team.

questions: Does cannabis cause psychosis, or could something else explain the link?
answers.short: Not known. Part of the link seems to come from other differences between people.
answers.but: The gene studies only looked at ever trying cannabis, not at daily or strong use.

questions: Has schizophrenia become more common as more people used cannabis?
answers.short: Studies disagree: some places saw more psychosis over time, others no rise as use grew.
answers.but: We know these studies only through reviews, and changes in diagnosis can blur trends.

questions: Does the kind of ayahuasca ceremony matter for how it goes?
answers.short: Maybe a little. People who felt safer and better supported at their last ceremony recalled a bit less fear. They also reported fewer problems later.
answers.but: One survey: people rated the ceremony and how it went at the same time, looking back.

questions: How common are bad trips, and can problems last?
answers.short: Fairly common: 41 in 100 people who'd used psychedelics recalled at least one difficult trip. 5 in 100 said one had badly affected their daily life.
answers.but: That's one online survey, and people were looking back over their whole lives.

questions: Do some people feel MDMA more strongly than others?
answers.short: Yes. The biggest link was the amount per kilo of body weight. Given the same amount, lighter people got more per kilo, which went with stronger effects.
answers.but: That's one lab, with healthy volunteers in a hospital, most of them trying MDMA for the first time.

questions: Do some people feel LSD more strongly than others?
answers.short: In lab studies, the dose went most with how strong LSD felt. Mood and personality did too.
answers.but: The paper says which way each link goes, not how big it is.

questions: Which harm reduction services exist for benzos, and do they work?
answers.short: Drug checking, prescribed benzos and stricter rules exist. No study has shown whether they lower harm.
answers.but: The review did not judge how good the studies were, and most had no comparison group.

questions: How common is using drugs alone, and why do people do it?
answers.short: Very common: 76 in 100 people at harm reduction sites said they'd used alone at least once in the past week. The most-picked reason: it's easier and more comfortable at home.
answers.but: It's one survey in one part of Canada, of people who already went to these sites.

questions: Does CBD taken with THC change THC's effects?
answers.short: Studies disagree on CBD and THC; no reliable pattern has been shown across different conditions.
answers.but: The studies used different amounts and timings. Most were small, and earlier trials were read through a review.

questions: Do drug and alcohol problems develop faster in women than in men?
answers.short: Not shown for women in general. It was seen mostly in people in treatment.
answers.but: All these studies rest on memory. People said years later how old they were at each step.

questions: Are women less likely than men to get alcohol or drug treatment?
answers.short: For alcohol, somewhat less likely, mostly years after problems start. For drugs, about the same.
answers.but: The surveys are from the US, and people remembered dates years later.

questions: In drug or alcohol treatment, do women do as well as men?
answers.short: Most large studies found no difference between women and men once in treatment.
answers.but: This comes from two reviews by one research group; we have not read the studies themselves.

questions: Do genes and the home you grow up in shape drug problems?
answers.short: Both are linked: what comes from birth parents, and the home a child grows up in.
answers.but: One Swedish study. What birth parents pass on includes the pregnancy, not just genes.

questions: Do words about drug use change how others see a person?
answers.short: Yes, some do. People judged a person more harshly when their troubles were said to come from drug use, not a health concern.
answers.but: These are views given after one made-up story, not how people who use drugs are really treated.

questions: How often do people who use cocaine also drink or use cannabis?
answers.short: On average, about 3 in 4 also used alcohol, and 4 to 6 in 10 cannabis.
answers.but: These averages mix very different studies, from about 1 in 10 to nearly all.

questions: Can caffeine bring on panic attacks in people with panic disorder?
answers.short: About half had a panic attack after one big dose; none after a dummy.
answers.but: Most studies used one large amount. The review cannot show what ordinary smaller servings do.

questions: Does eating before drinking change blood alcohol?
answers.short: In 9 men, a meal just before drinking roughly halved peak blood alcohol.
answers.but: One small lab study of young men. It measured blood alcohol, without testing impairment.

questions: Do official counts miss heroin deaths?
answers.short: In the places studied, closer reviews linked more deaths to heroin than records did.
answers.but: Each review used its own rules for what counts as a heroin death.

questions: Do autopsies and drug tests change which deaths count as drug deaths?
answers.short: Sometimes: at one centre, about 10 in 100 suspected drug deaths had another cause.
answers.but: Only two US places have been studied, so other places may differ.

questions: Does starting drugs young go with drug problems later?
answers.short: People who started young more often had drug or drinking problems later on.
answers.but: Studies can't show that starting young is the cause. Much of the link runs in families.

questions: Does using cannabis lead to other drugs (the 'gateway' idea)?
answers.short: Not known. Cannabis usually comes first, but that does not prove it leads on.
answers.but: Shared risks and access to other drugs could still explain the cannabis link.

questions: How common is using several drugs, and why does it matter?
answers.short: Common among people who use illegal drugs. It makes one drug's effects hard to study.
answers.but: The numbers come second-hand from reviews. They vary a lot between groups and studies.

questions: Are cocaine deaths more common in hot weather, and why?
answers.short: In 1990s New York, hot days had about a third more cocaine overdose deaths.
answers.but: The study compared days, not people, and did not allow for season.

questions: How is a death counted as a drug death?
answers.short: Different lists use different rules, so they do not always count the same deaths.
answers.but: The matching studies cover three places. The newest linked data are from 2012.

questions: Does it matter whether a coroner or a medical examiner investigates?
answers.short: Not clear. Coroner areas recorded deaths less precisely, but switching showed no clear change.
answers.but: No study checked which records were right, and the study of switching used data up to 1998.

questions: Can a blood level show that a drug caused death?
answers.short: Not on its own. Levels overlap between deaths with different causes.
answers.but: The rules and tests used to decide the cause also affect the comparison.

questions: Do health workers see and treat people who use drugs differently?
answers.short: Many health workers said they felt negative. Whether care was worse is not clear.
answers.but: Mostly surveys of what workers said, from 2000 to 2011, in a few countries.

questions: Is the risk of dying highest just after leaving prison?
answers.short: Yes. In the first week out, the risk of dying was about 1.5 to 2 times that of later weeks. Drug or alcohol poisoning was the top recorded cause.
answers.but: It's death records only: they don't name the drugs, and nobody measured tolerance, so the study can't say why.

questions: Do people recover from drug or alcohol problems, even without treatment?
answers.short: Many do. For alcohol, many people who recovered were never treated. In a US survey, 64 in 100 adults with alcohol dependence no longer counted as dependent about 3 years later.
answers.but: How many depends on who is counted, and in the studies we read, recovery without treatment was measured only for alcohol.

questions: What did the 'Rat Park' studies show about environment and morphine?
What did the 'Rat Park' studies show about environment and drugs?
answers.short: Less than is often said. Rats living together drank less morphine water, but only in some tests.
answers.but: All of this was in rats, so it says nothing direct about people.

questions: Will people who use cocaine choose another reward instead?
answers.short: Sometimes. Six people picked $5 over real cocaine doses about 1 time in 3 or 4.
answers.but: Only six people, in a lab, and cocaine was never offered without another choice.

questions: Does believing you've had alcohol change how you act?
answers.short: In lab tests, partly: believing they drank alcohol made men drink more.
answers.but: Lab tests from the 1970s and 1980s; the drinking test lasted 15 minutes, with low blood alcohol.

questions: How fast does cocaine act, and for how long?
answers.short: Smoked or injected, the high peaks in about a minute and fades within 30 minutes.
answers.but: Small lab studies of men who used cocaine often. Snorting was not measured.

questions: Is crack more addictive or more harmful than powder?
answers.short: Possibly, though it's the same drug. People new to crack reported each sign of dependence more often: about 18 to 32 in 100, against 5 to 12 for powder.
answers.but: Each person was asked once, so the surveys cannot show that crack itself is the reason.

questions: How fast can you get hooked on cocaine?
answers.short: Within a year of starting, about 5 in 100 who used only powder were dependent; 22 in 100 who went on to crack.
answers.but: People answered once, about themselves. The survey cannot show that crack itself made the difference.

questions: What is levamisole in cocaine, and what harm can it do?
answers.short: An animal worm medicine often found in cocaine, linked to blood and skin harm.
answers.but: This comes from case reports, so how often it causes harm is unknown.

questions: How common is cocaine psychosis among people treated for cocaine use?
answers.short: 68 in 100 people treated for cocaine reported psychotic symptoms; 16 in 100 had a diagnosed disorder.
answers.but: These were people in treatment, and many also used alcohol or other drugs.

questions: Do stimulant medicines help people stop using cocaine?
answers.short: In nine trials up to 2006, they did no better than a dummy pill.
answers.but: The trials were small, and newer reviews of these medicines have not been read yet.

questions: Why do people take ketamine, and what do they want from it?
answers.short: Most said: for its effects, like melting into their surroundings, and for fun.
answers.but: These 202 people were not picked at random, so their reasons may not be everyone's.

questions: How much more likely are people with problem cocaine use to die?
answers.short: Each year, 5 to 62 in 1,000 died: 4 to 8 times others their age.
answers.but: All groups injected, smoked crack daily, were in treatment or arrested; none only snorted.

questions: How often is chest pain after cocaine a heart attack?
answers.short: US studies looked at people in hospital with chest pain after cocaine. About 1 to 6 in 100 were having a heart attack.
answers.but: These were 1990s studies, and their blood tests could miss small heart attacks.

questions: Does cocaine affect memory and thinking?
answers.short: On average, people with cocaine problems score somewhat lower on memory and attention tests.
answers.but: No one was tested before they started, so we can't tell if cocaine caused the gap.

questions: Does cocaine narrow heart arteries, and do beta-blockers make it worse?
answers.short: Yes, in a lab cocaine narrowed heart arteries a little. After a beta-blocker, blood flow fell further in all 10 patients, but its effect on heart attacks is unknown.
answers.but: No trial has ever tested beta-blockers for chest pain after cocaine.

questions: Is using ketamine linked to bladder problems?
answers.short: Ketamine is linked to bladder problems seen in over 4,000 patients. In one survey, about 1 in 4 people who used it blamed it for urine problems.
answers.but: No study compared how often people who use ketamine and people who don't get these problems. So none can show ketamine caused them.

questions: How many UK deaths were linked to ketamine, and what were they?
answers.short: In England, ketamine was found or named in 283 deaths from 1999 to 2019, about 30 a year lately. Most had other drugs found too.
answers.but: Finding ketamine after a death does not show it caused the death.

questions: Is ketamine as good as electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) for hard-to-treat depression?
answers.short: Two big trials disagree: a US trial found ketamine drips at least as good as ECT. But in Swedish hospital patients, 63 in 100 got well on ECT, against 46.
answers.but: Everyone knew whether they got ketamine or ECT, and the trials took different people, so nobody knows why they disagree.

questions: What side effects do people have from ketamine treatment for depression?
answers.short: With ketamine for depression, studies most often found headache and dizziness. Next came feeling unreal and higher blood pressure. Most soon passed.
answers.but: Only 12 of 60 studies checked again 2 weeks or more after the last dose, and just 5 checked the bladder.

questions: Did teen cannabis use rise after US states legalised it?
answers.short: Not in one big US study. After states made recreational cannabis legal, teens in school were a bit less likely to say they had used it in the past month.
answers.but: Just 7 states had surveys from both before and after the change, and only for its first few years.

questions: Does a CBD medicine reduce seizures in a severe childhood epilepsy?
answers.short: In two trials, a CBD medicine cut seizures in Dravet syndrome. Seizures at least halved in 43 to 49 in 100 children, against 26 to 27 on a dummy liquid.
answers.but: The maker ran both trials, and in its own backup checks the result did not always hold up.

questions: How often do people seek emergency treatment after magic mushrooms?
answers.short: About 2 in 1,000 people who had used magic mushrooms in the past year said they sought emergency treatment, in one big online survey. After LSD: 10 in 1,000.
answers.but: Volunteers answered an online survey about themselves; nobody checked their answers, and people who could not answer were not counted.

questions: How often do people seek emergency treatment after LSD?
answers.short: About 10 in 1,000 people who'd used LSD in the past year, and answered, said they'd sought emergency treatment, in one big online survey. After magic mushrooms: 2 in 1,000.
answers.but: Volunteers took an online survey about themselves. Nobody checked their answers, or if the drug was really LSD.

questions: What do people say they meet on DMT?
answers.short: Mostly a being, a guide, a spirit or an alien. 69 in 100 said it gave them a message. People who said they'd met God without drugs told similar stories.
answers.but: Only people who'd had such a meeting took part, so we can't tell how often it happens.

questions: Can a ketamine drip lift depression within hours, and for how long?
answers.short: It can, within hours. A day after one drip, 64 in 100 were much better, against 28 in 100 after a sedative drip. For most, it faded within weeks.
answers.but: People can often tell they got ketamine, which may make the lift look bigger.

questions: Is cannabis stronger than it used to be?
answers.short: Yes, on average. In cannabis from 7 countries, 1970 to 2017, THC, its main active part, rose about 3 points every 10 years in weed and 6 in hash.
answers.but: Most samples were cannabis seized by police, not picked at random, so they may not match what people buy.

questions: Does cannabis make people lazy or unmotivated?
answers.short: In a London study, people using cannabis about 4 days a week felt no less motivated than people who had used it fewer than 10 times, and were as willing to work for sweets.
answers.but: A one-time snapshot of people using about 4 days a week: it can't show what cannabis does over years or with heavy daily use.

questions: Can other people's cannabis smoke make you fail a urine drug test?
answers.short: Rarely at the US government's workplace limit: after an hour in a smoky sealed room, 1 of 18 people who didn't smoke went over it. At a lower limit, 12 did.
answers.but: One small lab test in a sealed room, mostly in thick smoke; everyday smoke wasn't tested.

questions: Can eating poppy seeds make you fail a sports drug test?
answers.short: Yes, it can. In one study, all 9 people who ate poppy seed cake had morphine in their urine above the sports limit of the time.
answers.but: The cake used the strongest of 8 seed products tested, which had about 18 to 250 times more morphine than the rest.

questions: Do CBD products contain what their labels say?
answers.short: Mostly not. Of 84 CBD products bought online in the US in 2016, only about 3 in 10 matched their CBD label. About 1 in 5 also held THC.
answers.but: One test of products bought online in 2016; products sold in shops, or today, may differ.

questions: What happened after Portugal decriminalised all drugs?
answers.short: Mixed. Adults who'd ever tried a drug went from 8 to 12 in 100, but use in the last year barely moved. New HIV cases in people who use drugs fell.
answers.but: Treatment and other help grew too, starting in 1999, so these figures can't show what the law alone did.

questions: Do most US dollar bills carry traces of cocaine?
answers.short: In one US study, about 9 in 10 one-dollar bills had traces of cocaine. The typical bill held a little over a millionth of a gram.
answers.but: One small study of 50 US one-dollar bills collected by 2000. Cocaine on money today, or elsewhere, may differ.

questions: Can drugs be ranked by how much harm they do?
answers.short: Experts have tried: a UK panel ranked alcohol most harmful overall, mostly for harm to other people. For the person using, crack, heroin and meth scored worst.
answers.but: The scores are one panel's views, not measures, and alcohol's top score partly reflects how many people drink.

questions: Did the original DARE school programme stop young people using drugs?
answers.short: No. Across 11 studies of the original DARE school classes, kids who had DARE said they used alcohol, tobacco and illegal drugs about as much as kids who didn't.
answers.but: Only the original classes were tested: DARE was rebuilt in 2001, and that version wasn't part of this review.

questions: Did the US government's anti-drug ads stop teens using cannabis?
answers.short: No sign they did. Despite nearly $1 billion from Congress, teens' reported cannabis use stayed flat in a national survey, and those who remembered more ads weren't less likely to start.
answers.but: Nearly every teen saw the ads, so there was no group without them to compare cannabis use with.

questions: Does coffee dehydrate you?
answers.short: Not in a 3-day test. Men who drink coffee daily peed 2.41 litres a day on coffee days and 2.43 on water days.
answers.but: One 3-day test in 50 men who already drank coffee daily, too small to rule out a small effect.

questions: Do 'smart drugs' like Adderall make healthy people smarter?
answers.short: Barely. A single pill of Adderall (amphetamine) or methylphenidate gave healthy adults at most a small lift on some lab tests. In one trial, people felt helped; scores didn't rise.
answers.but: These studies tested a single pill in a lab, in healthy volunteers. Daily use, studying and exams were not tested.

questions: Do benzodiazepines cause dementia?
answers.short: Not known. In Quebec health records, long use of benzodiazepines was linked to Alzheimer's. A Seattle study that tested people found no clear link with the heaviest use.
answers.but: Neither study could rule out that early dementia, which can bring worry and poor sleep, led to the prescriptions.

questions: Why do people use kratom, and what do they say it does?
answers.short: Mostly for pain, anxiety or depression, people told two surveys, and most felt it helped. In one, about 4 in 10 had used kratom to cut down or stop opioids.
answers.but: Both surveys reached people mostly through a pro-kratom group, and those who quit after bad experiences were left out of one and may be too few in the other.

questions: How often is kratom found in overdose deaths?
answers.short: Kratom turned up in about 6 of every 1,000 overdose deaths in 27 US states in 2016–17. It was almost always found with other drugs.
answers.but: Testing for kratom varied and was not recorded, so some deaths with kratom were probably missed.

questions: Does psilocybin help depression?
answers.short: It may. In one trial, 42 in 100 given psilocybin kept their depression score at least halved from week 1 to week 6, against 11 in 100 given a vitamin pill.
answers.but: People could probably tell they had taken psilocybin, and nobody checked, which may have made the gap look bigger.

questions: Is psilocybin better than a standard antidepressant for depression?
answers.short: Not shown. In one trial of 59 people, psilocybin and the antidepressant escitalopram showed no clear difference in depression, at 6 weeks or 6 months.
answers.but: The trial was too small to show they work equally well, and people expected nearly twice as much from psilocybin.

questions: Does alcohol kill brain cells?
answers.short: In one study, men who drank alcohol heavily for years had about as many nerve cells in the brain's outer layer as other men: about 23 billion each.
answers.but: Only the outer layer was counted, in 22 men, so it can't say what heavy drinking does to other areas.

questions: Is moderate drinking linked to changes in the brain?
answers.short: In one UK study, people who drank more alcohol more often had a memory area rated 'shrunken' on a scan. So did 35 in 100 who barely drank.
answers.but: Each brain was scanned once, so the study shows a link, not shrinking, and not that alcohol caused it.

questions: Can psilocybin bring on a mystical experience, and does it last?
answers.short: It can: most people in one lab study scored as having a full mystical experience. Two months later, 67 in 100 ranked it among their 5 most meaningful experiences.
answers.but: Everyone in that study already took part in religious or spiritual activities, which may have made them see it as more spiritual.

questions: Does caffeine make you sharper, or just undo withdrawal?
answers.short: In one lab study, caffeine made everyone faster. But those who often have it only got as alert as those who rarely do.
answers.but: Only one study, and people chose their own caffeine habits, so something else about them could explain it.

questions: Do people describe ketamine trips the way others describe near-death experiences?
answers.short: More than for any other drug, going by the words alone: of 165 drugs, ketamine trip reports read most like near-death accounts. Salvia and LSD came close behind.
answers.but: Only words were compared. Nobody showed the trips and the near-death experiences feel alike.

questions: Can psilocybin help people drink less?
answers.short: Maybe. In one trial, people given psilocybin with talk therapy drank heavily on about 10 in 100 days, against 24 with a comparison pill.
answers.but: Almost everyone could tell if they got psilocybin, and people reported their own drinking.

questions: Can psilocybin help people quit smoking?
answers.short: Not known. In one small study, 12 of 15 people given psilocybin plus lots of counselling weren't smoking 6 months later.
answers.but: There was no comparison group, so no one can tell what psilocybin added to all the counselling.

questions: Is using LSD, mushrooms or mescaline linked to mental health problems?
answers.short: People who had used LSD, mushrooms or mescaline reported mental health problems 2 to 3 times as often. The gap vanished once other drug use and life stress were counted.
answers.but: People were asked once, so the survey can't show whether LSD, mushrooms or mescaline cause or prevent problems.

questions: Is drinking coffee linked to better or worse health?
answers.short: Mostly better: in studies that followed people for years, people who drank coffee died a bit less often. In pregnancy, and for women's bones, the links went the other way.
answers.but: These studies only watched people, and gene studies found no sign that coffee itself lowers the risk of dying.

questions: Does giving out naloxone kits prevent opioid overdose deaths?
answers.short: Naloxone kits are linked to fewer deaths from heroin and other opioids, but it's not proven. At least 96 in 100 people given naloxone by someone trained survived.
answers.but: Surviving doesn't prove naloxone saved a life, since most overdoses aren't fatal, and only one study compared death rates.

questions: Is nitrous oxide (laughing gas) linked to nerve damage?
answers.short: Yes: doctors have described nerve damage after nitrous oxide (laughing gas). In an online survey, about 4 in 100 people who used it in the past year reported lasting numbness.
answers.but: No doctor checked these answers and people chose to take part, so it can't show how common lasting numbness is after nitrous oxide.

questions: Do supervised injection sites reduce overdose deaths?
answers.short: Not proven: near Vancouver's site for injecting heroin, cocaine and other drugs, overdose deaths fell about a third after it opened. Elsewhere in the city, about a tenth.
answers.but: Just one site, before and after, and nothing else was ruled out, such as extra police.

questions: Does microdosing magic mushrooms do anything, or is it placebo?
answers.short: In two trials, people could feel a magic mushroom or LSD microdose on the day. But their mood and thinking were not clearly better than with a dummy capsule.
answers.but: Only a small one-week trial used just magic mushrooms; the bigger one was mostly LSD, and neither lasted months.

questions: Does esketamine nasal spray work for hard-to-treat depression?
answers.short: In two big trials, esketamine spray (a form of ketamine) did a little better than a dummy spray. Only one trial passed its main test.
answers.but: About 1 in 4 felt detached or unreal on esketamine, so many may have known which spray they got, and nobody asked.

questions: Can touching fentanyl make you overdose?
answers.short: Poison experts call it very unlikely for police and paramedics, and no overdose from touching fentanyl has been confirmed. In 214 news stories about exposed responders, none had proof.
answers.but: Nobody has measured real touches, and finding no proven case is not proof it never happens.

questions: Do police believe touching fentanyl can cause overdose? Does training change that?
answers.short: In three US surveys, about 4 in 5 police and other first responders thought touching fentanyl could cause an overdose or death. Right after trainings, far fewer did.
answers.but: No survey picked people at random. Answers came right after training, with no untrained group or later check.

questions: Does LSD damage your chromosomes?
answers.short: Studies from 1967 to 1970 found no clear rise in broken chromosomes after pure LSD. Early reports of more breaks came mostly from people using many drugs.
answers.but: Small studies that only looked at blood cells under a microscope; the best had no group without LSD.

questions: Do trips show you the truth, or just change your beliefs?
answers.short: These studies can't say if it's the truth. But after a retreat, beliefs shifted a bit, towards ideas like other worlds and a conscious universe. The shift was still there 6 months later.
answers.but: The main study had no comparison group, and only 122 of over 800 people answered every survey. Most already leaned that way.

questions: Can psilocybin change your personality?
answers.short: Not proven. After psilocybin, people rated themselves about 3 to 5 points more 'open' 1 to 3 months later, on a scale where the average adult scores 50.
answers.but: These were people rating themselves before and after, and no study checked that against how they acted. The one test against another drug found no difference.

questions: Why do psychedelic visuals look like tunnels, spirals and honeycombs?
answers.short: Maybe the visual brain's own wiring. A maths model shows how tunnels, spirals, cobwebs and honeycombs could arise there. It wasn't tested in people on a drug.
answers.but: It's only maths: the drug is just a setting for how excitable the brain is. The match was judged by eye against a few drawings.

questions: What does MDMA do to sex drive, erections and orgasm?
answers.short: People say desire often goes up, erections can go either way, and orgasm often takes longer. In one survey, 8 of 20 men said erections got weaker on MDMA, and 8 stronger.
answers.but: It's 35 people who chose to talk about it, remembering past experiences. Nobody tested their pills.

questions: How is MDA different from MDMA?
answers.short: It seemed to last longer, with more visuals and less anxiety: at 6 hours MDA was still clearly felt and MDMA wasn't. That's one small lab study.
answers.but: MDA and MDMA weren't tested on the same people. The MDMA results, from other people in earlier studies, stop at 6 hours.

questions: LSD or mushrooms: what's actually different?
answers.short: Mostly how long it lasts: about 9 to 11 hours for LSD, 6 to 7 for psilocybin, the drug in mushrooms. Otherwise 28 lab volunteers rated the trips alike on most measures.
answers.but: Finding no difference in 28 people doesn't prove there is none. And most could tell which drug they'd had.

questions: What happens when you mix MDMA with alcohol?
answers.short: People felt just as drunk as on alcohol alone, but less sleepy, and test scores fell about as far. Blood MDMA peaked 13% higher, in a lab study of 9 men.
answers.but: Only 9 men, in a lab. Heart measurements were taken but never reported.

questions: What if I take LSD and MDMA at the same time?
answers.short: Blood pressure and heart rate went higher than on LSD alone, and bad feelings weren't clearly eased. In a lab study of 24 people, top blood pressure was 13 points higher.
answers.but: Healthy people took one amount of each, in a calm hospital room. Nothing serious happened, but 24 people can't show rare dangers.

questions: Are fake pills with fentanyl getting more common?
answers.short: Yes, in US records to 2021. Overdose deaths with signs of fake pills rose from 2 to about 5 in 100, and to about 15 in 100 in western states.
answers.but: These are police and death records, which can't show what share of street pills hold fentanyl. Death records likely miss many fake pills.

questions: Would I know if someone was overdosing on opioids?
answers.short: Not always. On a written test, people trained by overdose programmes spotted about 7 of 9 opioid overdoses. People without that training spotted about 5 of 9.
answers.but: It was a paper test with 62 people that staff picked, not real overdoses. Nobody was tested before training, so training may not be the reason.

questions: Can using in a new place make an overdose more likely?
answers.short: Maybe. In rats, heroin was more often deadly in a new place. In people, nobody has tested it well. One study asked 10 overdose survivors what was different.
answers.but: That's 10 people's memories, about 5 years later, with nobody to compare them with. Only 3 of them recalled a new place or crowd.

questions: Is it dangerous to stop methadone or buprenorphine (Suboxone)?
answers.short: Deaths were more common off treatment, most of all in the first 4 weeks after leaving. In 16 methadone studies, about 36 in 1,000 died a year off treatment, against 11 on it.
answers.but: These studies counted everyone who left, for any reason. People who leave differ in other ways, so the studies can't show that stopping itself caused the deaths.

questions: Can opioid withdrawal itself kill you?
answers.short: Deaths have been reported, but nobody knows how often. One editorial lists 11, all in jail. It suggests vomiting and diarrhoea, left untreated, can dry the body out until the heart fails.
answers.but: It's one editorial's list, built from news reports and a court case. With no count of how many people went through withdrawal, there's no rate.

questions: Do indica and sativa labels tell you what's in your weed?
answers.short: Mostly not. In 41,201 lab-tested US weed samples, indica, hybrid and sativa labels barely matched the mix of terpenes, the compounds behind weed's smell. Strain names did a bit better.
answers.but: The labels came from a strain website, not the bags. And nobody measured how the weed made people feel.

questions: How can I get a family member who refuses help into treatment?
answers.short: Family skills training called CRAFT worked best in trials. In one, 64 in 100 relatives who'd refused help started treatment, against 30 with confrontation training and 13 with counselling to join Al-Anon.
answers.but: Just four small US trials, and two came from a team that includes CRAFT's developer.

questions: Is it dangerous to stop benzos suddenly?
answers.short: It can be: two expert reviews warn of life-threatening seizures, but not how often. The only count they give is 2 of 11 prisoners on very high doses, in 1961.
answers.but: These are expert reviews, not studies. Their seizure warnings give no rates, and one gives no source for them.

questions: Do police and sniffer dogs at festivals stop people taking drugs?
answers.short: Not by much, going by what people said. With sniffer dogs, 66 in 100 said they'd still use drugs, against 77 with no police, in an Australian online survey.
answers.but: It's what people said they'd do at a made-up festival, not what they really did.
